text: Build job 6 of the records-history plan (docs/design/records-history.md section 9, decision D111): incremental checking. After a passing attribution check, write a checkpoint record to athena/records (the record type exists in athena-data history.rs) naming the last passing main commit, the records-branch tip it was judged against, and the check's version; a later check judges only main's commits and records added since the newest checkpoint. A full replay mode ignores checkpoints, judges everything from the start, and fails if it disagrees with the newest checkpoint; the CI attribution job runs incrementally on pushes and as a full replay on its weekly schedule. Report per run the seconds taken and the number of commits and records judged. Tests: the incremental run judges only the new commits; a tampered checkpoint (one that names a commit the full replay fails) is caught by the replay; a check-version change forces a full replay. Measure on this repository: time a full replay and an incremental run one landing behind, and put both numbers in the CHANGELOG entry, marked measured.
